title: Adventure Engine
tagline: You make your program choose what happens next.
objectives: Write an if line and an else line, so my program does one thing or the other.
Add a third road with elif.
Test my room by trying every word a player could type, not just the one I expect.

config.headline: Today your program chooses what happens next.
lines: Every program you have written so far runs its lines in order, from the top to the bottom, and it does the same thing every time. Today you write a program that CHOOSES. It reads what the player typed, and then it decides which lines to run.

You are going to build a text adventure. A text adventure is a story that a program tells you one piece at a time. It asks you what to do, you type your answer, and what happens next depends on what you typed.

Here is one room of a text adventure, playing on its own further down this card. The room asks one question. What happens next depends on the answer, and each thing that can happen next is called a road. The player typed the word trolley, so the room chose the trolley road. Watch it once.

The whole class is building one adventure today. It is set in this school after the bell has gone: everybody has gone home, the doors are still open, and odd things happen. Each of you writes ONE room — a place in the school, one question, and two roads the player can take. When your room is finished, it joins the class's adventure, and you can play it, going through rooms your classmates wrote.
Here is what happens in the next hour, in the order it happens.
1. First you watch a short film. It has no sound.
2. Then you do three training builds — three short practice jobs. In the first you fix a room somebody else wrote. In the second you put a room in order. In the third you add a third road to a room.
3. Then you write your own room. The website checks every road in it before it joins the adventure.

4. Then you play the class adventure. You go through five rooms, one after another. Each room was written by a classmate, or it is one of the rooms from the training builds. Nobody's name is shown on any room — each room has a number instead.
5. After that there is a screen with four small extra jobs on it. They are there if you want them, and none of them is marked.
The hour ends with one marked question and the How did it go? screen.

builds.goalLine: Write one room of the class adventure: a place in this school, one question, two roads, and a door for anything else the player types.

features.label: If the player types your SECOND word, the other road runs and ends with a door line.
features.nudge: Look at the word in speech marks on your elif line. It must match your second word exactly, and its road needs a NEXT: door line.

features.label: If the player types anything else, the room still sends them through a door.
features.nudge: The banana test: the player typed banana, and your room had no road for it. The else road catches every word you did not plan for — check it is there, and that it ends with a door line.

features.label: The two roads tell different stories.
features.nudge: Both roads print the same words. Give each road its own story line.

builds.goalLine: Give one road a twist: a second question, with its own if and else, pushed in under that road.
builds.brief:
Your room is still there, in the box you type in.
1. Pick one road.
2. Under that road's story line, add a second question with input( ). Give its answer a new name. In the shape, that line is: twist = input( a second question )
3. Under that question, add an if line and an else line. They belong to the road, so push them in FOUR spaces, the same as the road's story line. The if line asks about the new name. In the shape, it is: if twist == "a word":
4. Under the twist's if line, put a door line. Under the twist's else line, put another door line. Those two lines belong to the twist, so push them in EIGHT spaces — four for the road, four more for the twist.
5. The road's old door line is not needed now. The twist's two door lines take its place, so take the old one out.
shape: print( what happens on that road )
builds.shapeNote: A fork inside a road is pushed in twice: four spaces for the road, four more for the twist.

check.usesSay: It ran, but there is no second fork pushed in under a road yet. The twist is an if and an else with eight spaces in front of them.

builds.matchedSay: It runs, and one of your roads forks again. A fork inside a fork is called a nested if.
builds.notYetSay: It is not working yet. Read the console. A twist needs eight spaces in front of its if and its else, and each part of the twist needs a door line.
builds.runCheckedSay: The twist is yours, so this card cannot tell you the exact words to expect. Press RUN, take the road with the twist in it, and answer the second question.
builds.finishLabel: Finish this part and carry on

config.help:
This card comes in two parts. First you get ready, then you write your room.

1. Read the five jobs your room has to do, and watch the film.
2. Type the two words your player will be able to type. Your question must say them.
3. Press Start writing.
4. Click a line on the right to put it in your room, then change its CAPITAL words. Or press Put the shape in for me and change every CAPITAL word.
5. Press RUN my room and play it. The path check under the five jobs shows which words reached a door.
6. When all five jobs say done, press Publish my room to the class adventure.

I can test my room by trying each of my two words, and then a word I did not plan for.

errorWords.name: Python does not know a box (a variable) with that name. Check the spelling matches the box name on the input( ) line.
errorWords.type: You have joined a number onto words with a +. Put the number inside speech marks, or wrap it with str( ).
errorWords.badinput: Python could not read that line. Check three things. A fork line asks its question with two equals signs: ==. Every if, elif and else line ends with a colon. The lines that belong under an if, an elif or an else are pushed in by four spaces.
errorWords.eof: Something was opened on that line and never closed. Look for a bracket or a speech mark with no partner.
errorWords.unindent: The lines under the fork are not lined up. Every line that belongs to an if, an elif or an else starts exactly four spaces in — no more and no less.
errorWords.timelimit: Your program was still going after a few seconds, so the website stopped it. Press RUN again. If it happens a second time, tell whoever is in the room.
errorWords.other: Python stopped at the line named above. Read that line again, slowly, and check every bracket and every speech mark.

builds.title: Job 1 — the password door
builds.whiff: A door that opens for one exact word, and stays shut for everything else.
builds.goalLine: Build a door that opens only when the player types the password you choose.
builds.brief: This is a fork with one road and an else. The password is a word you choose. The two equals signs, ==, check whether what the player typed is EXACTLY that word, capital letters included.

lines.t: print("A door with a keypad. It wants a word.")

blanks.label: the password — any word you like

lines.t: print("Nothing happens. The keypad blinks red.")

builds.matchedSay: It runs. Try the password, then run it again and try the same word with a capital letter. The two equals signs only match the exact word, capital letters included.
builds.runCheckedSay: The password is yours, so this card cannot tell you what to expect. Press RUN, type the password, then run it again and type something else.

builds.title: Job 2 — four roads
builds.whiff: A room with four roads: if, elif, another elif, and else.
builds.goalLine: Add a third word and a third road to this room, so it has four roads in all.
builds.brief: A room can have as many elif roads as you like. Python checks them from the top and takes the FIRST one whose word matches.
fixedTop: print("You are in the gym. The lights hum.")
choice = input("Do you take the ball, the rope or the ____? Type ball, rope or ____.")
print("You bounce it once. The echo goes on for a very long time.")
print("You climb three metres and decide that is plenty.")
builds.fixedTopLabel: Already written — fill the gaps in the question with your third word

fixedBlanks.label: your third word, in both gaps of the question

blanks.label: what happens on the third road

lines.t: print("You stand in the middle of the gym. The lights hum louder.")

builds.matchedSay: Your room has four roads now, and Python takes the first one whose word matches.
builds.runCheckedSay: The third word is yours, so this card cannot tell you what to expect. Press RUN and try all three words. Then try a word that is not in the question.

builds.title: Job 3 — the player's name
builds.whiff: Ask the player's name first, and use it in the story.
builds.goalLine: Ask the player's name before the question, and put it into what the room says.
builds.brief: Asking the player's name and using it is what you learned in Lesson 3. Now it goes inside a room. input( ) keeps the name in a box (a variable), and the + sign joins the name onto words.

lines.t: name = input("Before we start — what is your name?")
print("You are in the ICT room, " + name + ". Every screen is on, and every screen shows your name.")
choice = input("Do you sit down or run? Type sit or run.")
print("The nearest screen says: hello again, " + name + ".")
print("You run. Behind you, every screen goes off at once.")
print("You are in the ICT room, " + "name" + ".")

builds.matchedSay: It works, and the room used the name the player typed.
builds.notYetSay: Not yet. If the room printed the word name instead of the name you typed, look for a line where name is inside speech marks — that line is the mistake.
builds.runCheckedSay: The name is whatever you type, so this card cannot tell you the exact words to expect. Press RUN, type a name, then type sit.
builds._provenance: DFM 197 14 Sep 2026: usesReplies true → [0] — a fork room never echoes the CHOICE word, so "every reply must come back out" could not be passed; the NAME (reply 0) is what the job is about

builds.title: Job 4 — a room from nothing
builds.whiff: Write a whole room yourself, from nothing. There are no ready-made lines this time.
builds.goalLine: Write a whole room from nothing: a place, one question, two roads and an else.
builds.brief: There are no lines to click this time. If you get stuck, the Show me the shape button is still there.
shape: <box> = input( the question — and the two words to type )
print( what happens on that road )
print( what happens on the other road )
print( what happens for anything else )
builds.shapeNote: Every road ends with its own door line, pushed in under it.

check.usesSay: It ran, but a whole room needs a question with input( ), an if road, an else road, and a NEXT: door line on every road.

builds.matchedSay: You wrote a whole room from nothing. It is a real program, and you wrote every word of it.
builds.runCheckedSay: Every word here is yours, so this card cannot tell you what to expect. Press RUN and play your room.
